Change Prediction Method

The Change Prediction Method as the engine runs it: twelve subsystems with their share of a new vehicle's development effort, the links through which a change propagates, the thresholds and the add-ons, and the back-test against documented BMW decisions. Every weight and link is the team's assumption, not calibrated; the engine records the model hash with every estimate.

Reference
Clarkson, Simons, Eckert (2004), Predicting Change Propagation in Complex Design, Journal of Mechanical Design 126(5) https://oro.open.ac.uk/18626
Engine
backend/tracepoint/effort/cpm.py, model file config/effort/model.yaml
Model hash
789fcb7624b8 (assumption, not calibrated)
Thresholds
adapt below 15 %, major revision up to 50 %, new generation from there; a K3 change without carryover is a new generation regardless of the score.
Certification add-on
12 % once per package when a change of at least 30 % own impact starts in Body/structure, Powertrain, HV battery.
On this vehicle
Platform FAAR (front-wheel-drive compact). The model keeps HV battery, Charging off this vehicle; the weights of the others are renormalised to 100. All F70 variants in the German catalogue are ICE or 48 V MHEV. The link matrix was written for CLAR and is reused as an assumption; FAAR-specific links are not calibrated.

Rules of the engine

Carryover
A change the portfolio already holds, or that the platform was prepared for, spreads to its neighbours with 30 % of the usual likelihood.
Smaller changes
The link likelihoods describe a change of own impact 0.3 (a module change); a smaller change spreads proportionally less.
Platform rule
Replacing Body/structure, HV battery, Powertrain, E/E architecture to 80 % or more without carryover is a platform change (K3) and means a new generation.
Configuration
A configuration change (K0) stays within own impact 0.1 and does not spread.
Propagation paths
A change spreads over at most 3 links.
Size classes
XS below 1 %, S below 5 %, M below 15 %, L below 50 %, XL from 50 %

Links between the subsystems

Rows: where a change starts. Columns: what it reaches. A cell carries the likelihood that a change in the row forces a change in the column and the share of the column's design redone if it does; the fill follows the likelihood. Only pairs with a physical or functional interface have a link; the interface is named on hover and in the list beneath.
